questions.q: What is the honest difference between a Kafka topic and a Fabric Eventstream, per this lesson?
options: A topic can only hold one event at a time
Eventstreams support replay while Kafka topics do not
A topic is a first-class object you name, partition, and set retention on directly, while an Eventstream is a managed pipeline object with those details abstracted away
They are functionally identical with no configuration differences
questions.explain: Fabric handles partitioning and retention underneath an Eventstream without surfacing them as tunable settings the way Kafka does with a topic.

questions.q: How does Kafka's consumer group protocol compare to how Fabric handles parallel consumption of an Eventstream?
options: Fabric requires manually configuring a consumer group identical to Kafka's
Fabric and Kafka use the exact same underlying protocol

A Kafka consumer group is a protocol you interact with directly by writing consumers that join it, while Fabric handles parallel consumption as part of its managed runtime with no equivalent group-membership concept
Kafka has no concept of parallel consumption at all
questions.explain: This is one of the concrete places Kafka exposes something as a first-class concept that Fabric abstracts away entirely.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where is Fabric's Eventstream genuinely simpler than any Kafka path, even Confluent Cloud?
options: Fabric cannot process any real-time data
Eventstreams have no connectors of any kind
Fabric requires more manual infrastructure setup than self-hosted Kafka
There's no cluster, broker count, partition count, or replication factor to configure at all
questions.explain: Even Kafka's easiest managed path still involves a cluster concept and sizing decisions; a fully managed Eventstream has none of that.

questions.q: Where is Kafka genuinely more flexible than Fabric's Eventstreams, per this lesson?
options: Kafka is always cheaper than Fabric in every scenario
It's vendor-neutral, runs anywhere including on-prem or any cloud, and has a much larger connector ecosystem not tied to one vendor's roadmap
Kafka only works inside the Azure ecosystem
Kafka requires zero operational effort to run
questions.explain: That vendor-neutrality and ecosystem size is real value for teams spanning multiple clouds or integrating with existing Kafka systems.

questions.q: What does Kafka Connect's connector ecosystem offer that Eventstream's built-in connectors don't, according to this lesson?
options: Eventstream connectors work outside of Fabric entirely
A much larger, vendor-neutral set of hundreds of source/sink connectors across many vendors, versus Fabric's own curated set
Kafka Connect has no connectors at all, unlike Eventstreams
Kafka Connect only supports a single database vendor
questions.explain: Both move data without custom code, but Connect's ecosystem is far larger and not tied to Fabric or any single vendor.
